scope_note: Corrective primary-source audit adds two county taxable-account observations, state-verified incentive-compliance thresholds, current operator-reported jobs and community funding, one county-received grant, facility electricity use, supporting renewable capacity, and the 2018 expansion forecast. The search trail covers identity, land use, permits, assessor and fiscal records, incentives, public costs, utilities, water, suppliers, courts, bonds, community funding, and federal county outcomes. Most public evidence covers the multi-building Henrico campus or Scout Development's county account and remains unallocated to the selected inventory building; overlapping funding and investment figures are not summed, and unavailable supplier payments, utility bills, tax receipts, incentive costs, payroll, and marginal public-service costs remain explicit gaps.

sources.title: Henrico officials join governor to announce plans for Facebook facility
sources.notes: The contemporaneous announcement describes a planned $750 million, 970,000-square-foot Facebook data center on approximately 300 acres at White Oak, more than 100 planned full-time jobs, a separate $250 million statewide solar commitment, and more than $40 million of preexisting county investment in park-wide infrastructure. The infrastructure amount is not project-allocable and is not encoded as a public cost.

sources.title: Henrico officials, governor announce major expansion of Facebook data center
sources.notes: The county announced a planned additional $750 million and three 500,000-square-foot buildings, bringing the program to five buildings and more than 2.4 million square feet. It projected approximately 1,500 construction jobs and more than 200 full-time operating jobs after completion; those forecasts are retained separately from later reported actuals.

sources.title: Henrico Planning Commission agenda - POD2017-00431 Project Echo
sources.notes: The approved plan of development identifies Project Echo on part of parcel 849-704-6939 at Technology Boulevard and Portugee Road. Phase I comprised two connected one-story buildings with mechanical penthouses totaling approximately 1 million square feet; three future buildings totaled 1.5 million square feet on a roughly 328-acre M-2 site served by county water and sewer.

sources.title: Facebook's Henrico Data Center is officially online
sources.notes: The EDA reports the data center officially online, more than $1 billion invested, 1,500 construction jobs supported, and numerous local partners and suppliers. It also reports nearly $830,000 of pandemic-era support, including $475,000 for small businesses and nonprofits and $280,000 for public-school hotspots and food; the components are not added to the later cumulative operator total.

sources.title: Henrico County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2025
sources.notes: The principal-taxpayer table identifies Scout Development LLC as the company that bought and developed the site containing the Facebook data center and reports combined real- and personal-property assessed values of $2,045,241,378 for calendar 2024 and $2,364,906,425 for calendar 2025. The notes also describe 2017 and 2022 performance agreements covering facilities at 6200 and 7301 Technology Boulevard and state that grant amounts are confidential under Virginia law.

sources.title: VEDP Board of Directors public meeting book - Data Center Retail Sales and Use Tax Exemption performance
sources.notes: The DCRSUT project table lists Scout Development LLC in Henrico as a single-user project with a September 26, 2017 MOU and June 1, 2021 performance date. The project is marked post-performance and as having achieved the statutory minimums of 50 new jobs and $150 million of capital investment; the table does not disclose actual tax benefits or amounts above those thresholds.

sources.title: Meta Henrico Data Center information sheet
sources.notes: The current two-page operator factsheet reports more than $1 billion invested, 1,500 peak skilled-trade workers, more than 200 operational jobs supported, more than 200 grants and sponsorships since 2019, more than $4.2 million of direct local funding, and eight Virginia clean-energy projects adding 700 MW. It says Meta pays the full costs of energy and county water and wastewater service but publishes no bills, rates, or project-specific public-cost amounts.

sources.title: Henrico County June 2023 budget amendments
sources.notes: The county amendment appropriates $35,000 received through Meta Data Center Action Grants for public-library computer work-and-play stations. This recipient-reported amount is a component of broader Meta community funding and is not additive to the operator's cumulative total.

sources.title: Issued air permits for data centers
sources.notes: The issued-permit inventory lists Scout Development LLC, registration/application 52629-4, Henrico County, Piedmont region, Article 6 minor new-source review, issued June 27, 2019. The indexed record does not expose generator count, nameplate capacity, runtime, fuel use, emissions, or cost.

sources.title: Virginia State Corporation Commission 2019 Annual Report
sources.notes: The report says approved Dominion Schedule RF arrangements support Scout Development LLC/Facebook and apply to customers with at least 30 million kWh of incremental annual load. It describes renewable-energy-certificate purchases but discloses no Henrico-specific usage, demand, bill, rate impact, interconnection cost, or customer payment.

sources.title: Henrico County Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Approved Budget
sources.notes: The budget reports a $2 million General Fund Revenue (Facebook) allocation to school technology and lists White Oak-area utility capital projects, including the Portugee Road Water Pumping Station. It does not identify the revenue type, payer account, facility allocation, or any project-attributable share of system capital or annual public-service costs, so no fiscal or public-cost record is created.

sources.title: Henrico County real property search
sources.notes: The live search interface supports GPIN/PID and street-address queries. Exact identifiers 849-701-2260, 6200 Technology Boulevard, and 7301 Technology Boulevard were cross-checked against county board records, but no stable text-rendered current parcel detail or personal-property account was captured; fiscal values therefore rely on the audited principal-taxpayer table.

sources.title: Henrico County Board of Supervisors regular meeting minutes, February 11, 2025
sources.notes: A quitclaim and easement item states that Scout Development, LLC owns 6200 Technology Boulevard, GPIN 849-701-2260. The record confirms a current project-linked address and parcel identifier but reports no transfer price, assessment, construction cost, or inventory-building allocation.

sources.notes: The current rate page and linked utility materials were searched for Scout, Facebook, Meta, 6200 Technology Boulevard, and 7301 Technology Boulevard. They publish general schedules but no customer-level meter volumes, bills, capacity reservations, connection charges, marginal service cost, or discharge amount.

project_updates.title: Identity, opening, and evidence-scope search completed
project_updates.notes: Search family: operator facility identity and opening chronology. Query/identifier: Meta/Facebook Henrico Data Center, White Oak, August 5 2020; date range 2017-2026. Documents inspected: Meta opening page, current factsheet, county announcements, and planning records. Result: useful - confirms the campus was serving traffic by August 5, 2020, but public evidence generally covers the multi-building campus rather than the selected inventory footprint.
project_updates.project_description: Meta's Henrico Data Center is a hyperscale campus operated by Meta in White Oak Technology Park, Henrico County, Virginia; the inventory project represents one mapped building footprint, while public project evidence generally covers the campus. Henrico approved Project Echo in September 2017 as a phased 328-acre development with two connected Phase I buildings of about 1 million square feet and three future buildings totaling 1.5 million square feet, and construction began in October 2017. Meta reported the campus serving traffic on August 5, 2020; later county records distinguish 6200 Technology Boulevard from facilities at 7301 Technology Boulevard, so campus and later-building facts are not allocated to the selected footprint.

Result: useful - approved a roughly 328-acre, five-building phased program on county water/sewer; no phase-to-inventory-building crosswalk or cost schedule was published.
